picks.title: Pixel Watch 4 update adds Google's AI watch face generator
picks.rationale: Google's generative AI watch face creator, launched as a Pixel Watch 5 exclusive, now reaches last year's watch by update: a concrete release where generative AI is the feature itself.
picks.excerpt: Pixel Watch 4 update brings Google's generative AI watch face generator (previously a Pixel Watch 5 feature) to last year's watch, along with other additions.

picks.title: Pre-orders open for Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops, starting at $2,599
picks.rationale: Local-AI RTX Spark laptops move from announcement to purchasable: pre-orders are live from $2,599, with concrete Blackwell configurations to compare.
picks.excerpt: Pre-orders are now live for Nvidia RTX Spark laptops starting at $2,599; TechRadar picks three Blackwell-powered machines for running local AI.

picks.title: Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 review: Meta's new Muse model is the real upgrade
picks.rationale: A hands-on review of $449 AI glasses you can buy now. The hardware barely changed, so the story is the new Muse model running the on-glasses assistant.
picks.excerpt: Gizmodo reviews the $449 Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 AI glasses: same camera and AI feature set as before, but Meta's new Muse model is a significant upgrade to the on-glasses assistant; spatial audio arrives via the Meta AI app.

picks.title: One year with Alexa Plus: better at the smart home, not ready to run your life, and now with ads
picks.rationale: A year-long test of Amazon's generative-AI assistant on shipping Echo Show, Dot and Max hardware. It shows what the assistant does well and badly in daily use, and that it now carries ads.
picks.excerpt: A year living with Alexa Plus across Echo Show, Dot and Max: Amazon's generative-AI assistant is better at running the smart home, but not yet ready to run your life - and it now comes with ads.

picks.title: Xpanceo's AI smart contact lenses put 'an AI helper on your cornea' as soon as 2030
picks.rationale: The founders explain the prototype AI contact lenses they have built over five years and give a 2030 target date. The weakest pick (no shipping product yet), but it covers a new form factor not seen in the section before.
picks.excerpt: CNET interviews the founders of Dubai-based Xpanceo, which has spent five years building AI-powered smart contact lenses - 'an AI helper directly on your cornea' - that could arrive as soon as 2030.

https://www.techradar.com/pro/pre-orders.new_action: Pre-orders for RTX Spark laptops opened, with pricing from $2,599; the 10-08 card covered only the launch announcement. (history_match tag pointed at the 10-03 64GB DGX Spark card, a different product.)
